verdicts.verify_by: gno test -v -run TestB8TitleHomoglyphs in examples/gno.land/r/gnoland/store/v0 with tests/b8-lines-reach-catalog-store_test.gno copied in as b8_test.gno: expect every copy refused or title_taken, observe all five listed
verdicts.tldr: A look-alike of a listed title registers beside it when it swaps one glyph for a digit or punctuation mark of another script, or for an Arabic or Hebrew letter: the script-mixing check only counts letters, and titleKey folds none of these.
verdicts.details: validText sets foreign only on `case unicode.IsLetter(r) && !unicode.In(r, mixesWithLatin...)` (validate.gno:145), so a digit or punctuation mark of any script, Bengali U+09E6 or Hebrew paseq U+05C0, never counts as foreign. And Arabic alef and Hebrew samekh are letters of allowlisted scripts. foldRune (listing.gno:572-575) folds ASCII '0' to o and '|' to l but not their foreign twins, so 'Gn০land Swap' gets a different key from 'Gnoland Swap' while 'Gn0land Swap' collides with it. The ADR's T6 Residual names confusables outside the folds and leaves a full UTS #39 skeleton for later, so allowlisted letters such as alef fall under a risk the author accepted. The non-letter exemption does not: it breaks the 0 and | folds the code already ships, and the fix is cheap. Fix: give script-specific digits and punctuation the foreign check (or refuse every Nd outside ASCII and the allowlisted scripts next to Latin), and fold U+05C0, U+09E6 and U+0966 in foldRune.

verdicts.verify_by: gno test -v -run TestB8LatinExtBLookalikes with the same artifact: expect title_taken or bad_title, observe both listed
verdicts.tldr: A copy of a title written entirely in Latin, with LATIN CAPITAL IOTA standing for l or WYNN for p, registers beside the original because commonLatin lets in all of Latin Extended-B and titleKey folds neither letter.
verdicts.details: commonLatin is `r < 0x0250 && (r < 0x01C0 || r > 0x01C3) || ...` (validate.gno:177), so U+0196 Ɩ and U+01BF ƿ count as common Latin. The script-mixing check never fires because the title is pure Latin. strings.ToLower maps Ɩ to U+0269 ɩ, and foldRune has no case for it or for ƿ, so 'GnoƖand Pay' keys as gnoɩandpay against gnolandpay. Yet 'GnoIand Pay' with an ASCII I collides, since i folds to l. The code already drops U+01C0 to U+01C3 for this same look-alike reason, and the ADR says Latin letters outside the alphabets in common use are refused, which wynn is not. Fix: narrow commonLatin to the Extended-B letters the comment names (Romanian, Pinyin), or fold ɩ/Ɩ to l and ƿ to p in foldRune.

Base: the realm directory is absent at the merge base, so the behaviour is new in the diff.

verdicts.verify_by: gno test -v -run TestB8PickKeepsSwappedTagline with the artifact: expect picked() nil after the tagline or cover change, observe the pick kept
verdicts.tldr: After a GovDAO pick, the app can rewrite its tagline at once, and swap its cover a day later, while still showing under 'Picked by GovDAO'. This follows the ADR's design, which ends a pick only on hide, a kind change or a rename.
verdicts.details: picked() checks only `h < pick.until && l.shownApp() && titleKey(l.Title) == pick.title` (admin.gno:171). update() calls dropPick only when the folded title changes (listing.gno:228-229), so a Register with a new tagline keeps the pick, and render.gno:131 prints that tagline under the GovDAO heading. The ADR (§ pick, lines 369-372) lists the end triggers as hide, stopping being a shown app and rename, so the code does what the design says. Binding the tagline would also buy little, since the picked app's own realm, which the hero links to, can change freely after the vote. This is a scope choice for the author rather than a bug. Fix: if the pick should cover what GovDAO saw, record a hash of the tagline (and the effective cover) in setPick and compare it in picked(), or note in the ADR that the tagline and cover are not bound.
